interest: Shows postwar friction over SCAP's handling of Japan's silk trade, with Congress, Commonwealth buyers, and auction mechanics all in play.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.6225, filed under the classification for animal husbandry and silk culture in Japan) documents the rehabilitation, pricing, quota allocation, and international marketing of Japanese raw silk during the Allied Occupation between March 1946 and December 1948. Central matters include high-level coordination and inter-agency friction between the State Department, the War Department, and General Douglas MacArthur's SCAP headquarters over the status of civilian silk experts sent to Tokyo; the commercial distribution of Japanese silk stockpiles through the U.S. Commercial Company (USCC) via New York sealed-bid auctions and Japanese grading standards; inter-allied quota negotiations and currency exchange arrangements with Commonwealth nations including India, Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom; and late-1948 protests by American silk importers regarding price increases and large-scale French silk purchases financed indirectly through Marshall Plan funds.

subfiles.about: Representative Daniel J. Flood forwards to Edwin M. Martin a copy of his memorandum to General Hilldring concerning silk expert Magagna's mission to Japan.
subfiles.from: Daniel J. Flood, M.C., U.S. House of Representatives
subfiles.summary: Flood sends Martin his memo to Hilldring defending silk expert Magagna, thanking State for its cooperation.
subfiles.title: Letter from Daniel J. Flood to Edwin M. Martin enclosing memorandum to General Hilldring
subfiles.to: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Representative Daniel J. Flood urges General Hilldring to rectify SCAP's misunderstanding regarding silk expert Magagna's War Department affiliation and to end obstructionist interference by SCAP staff in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Daniel J. Flood, M.C., U.S. House of Representatives
subfiles.summary: Flood protests SCAP wrongly treating silk expert Magagna as State's man rather than the Army's, blaming 'amateur diplomats' on MacArthur's staff for blocking him.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Daniel J. Flood to Major General John H. Hilldring regarding Magagna's silk mission to SCAP
subfiles.to: Major General John H. Hilldring, Special Staff, War Department

subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges receipt of Representative Flood's inquiries concerning investigations into the Japanese silk mission.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Martin responds to Flood's inquiry on the Japanese silk mission, drafted by Whitman.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to Daniel J. Flood regarding Japanese silk mission inquiries
subfiles.to: Daniel J. Flood, M.C., U.S. House of Representatives

subfiles.about: The Board of Directors of the U.S. Commercial Company discusses whether to market Japanese raw silk through open auctions or sealed bids.
subfiles.from: C. W. Nichols, Division of International Resources, Department of State
subfiles.summary: USCC directors keep sealed-bid sales for Japanese silk rather than open auctions, citing satisfactory returns and avoiding premature price drops.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Sales of Japanese Silk by USCC Board of Directors

subfiles.about: India outlines its two-million-pound raw silk requirement from Japan and agrees to New Zealand's quota if debited against Australia's allocation.
subfiles.from: P. A. Menon, Secretary, India Supply Mission
subfiles.summary: Menon thanks Whitman for raising India's Japanese-silk quota to two million pounds, specifying grades and quantities needed.
subfiles.title: Letter from P. A. Menon to Roswell H. Whitman regarding Japanese raw silk allocations for India
subfiles.to: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: The State Department outlines the pricing formula for Japanese raw silk sales to India based on New York USCC auction returns minus shipping and insurance charges.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Whitman explains Japanese silk for India is priced off US auction results, minus freight and insurance costs.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to P. A. Menon regarding Japanese raw silk pricing and freight costs
subfiles.to: P. A. Menon, Secretary, India Supply Mission

subfiles.about: The India Supply Mission confirms its understanding regarding entitlements to purchase Japanese raw silk under announced percentage quotas.
subfiles.from: P. A. Menon, Secretary, India Supply Mission
subfiles.summary: Menon confirms India's understanding of its Japanese-silk purchase quota percentages.
subfiles.title: Letter from P. A. Menon to Roswell H. Whitman regarding Japanese raw silk purchase quotas
subfiles.to: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Roswell H. Whitman reports on an inquiry from the New Zealand Legation and submits a draft cable instructing SCAP on payment terms for silk sales to New Zealand.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Whitman drafts a telegram letting New Zealand buy Japanese silk on Australia's terms, pending sterling-conversion agreement.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Roswell H. Whitman proposing telegram to SCAP on silk sales to New Zealand
subfiles.to: A-H - JK Secretariat, Department of State

subfiles.about: R. O. Easton reports that War Department clearance has been obtained for the proposed terms of Japanese silk sales to New Zealand.
subfiles.from: R. O. Easton, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Easton tells Gross War Department clearance is secured for letting New Zealand buy silk on Australia's terms.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from R. O. Easton to Ernest A. Gross regarding silk sales to New Zealand
subfiles.to: Ernest A. Gross, Department of State

subfiles.about: The State Department instructs SCAP Tokyo to offer New Zealand the same silk sales and payment terms provided to Australia pending sterling convertibility agreements.
subfiles.summary: State tells SCAP to offer New Zealand the same silk-purchase terms as Australia, pending sterling convertibility.
subfiles.title: Telegram from State Department to SCAP Tokyo on terms of silk sales to New Zealand
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording British Embassy correspondence on pricing and charges for raw silk shipments from Japan to the United Kingdom.
subfiles.from: J. A. E. Smart, British Embassy, Washington
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Britain's Board of Trade asks how to calculate Japan f.o.b. silk prices from US auction results.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for letter from J. A. E. Smart regarding British raw silk purchases from Japan
subfiles.to: Roswell H. Whitman, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Attorney William S. Culbertson conveys client concerns regarding an impending Japanese silk price hike and large-scale French purchases funded under the Marshall Plan.
subfiles.from: William S. Culbertson, Culbertson, Aitchison & Briggs
subfiles.summary: Culbertson relays a silk importer's report that SCAP plans a 10% price hike and is favoring a discounted French purchase.
subfiles.title: Letter from William S. Culbertson to William J. McCornick regarding Japanese silk prices and French purchases
subfiles.to: William J. McCornick, Division of Commercial Policy, Department of State

subfiles.about: The State Department clarifies that it has no report of an impending Japanese silk price rise and is investigating reports of market preemption by French purchases.
subfiles.from: Merrill C. Gay, Assistant Chief, Division of Commercial Policy, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Gay tells Culbertson State has no confirmation of a Japanese silk price hike or French purchases blocking other buyers.
subfiles.title: Letter from Merrill C. Gay to William S. Culbertson regarding Japanese silk prices and French purchases
subfiles.to: William S. Culbertson, Culbertson, Aitchison & Briggs

subfiles.about: The State Department advises the British Embassy that f.o.b. Japan silk prices should be negotiated directly with SCAP in Tokyo and agrees to supply U.S. auction price lists.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Whitman tells Britain SCAP sets Japan silk pricing in Tokyo, promising to relay UK shipment terms and auction data.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to J. A. E. Smart regarding Japanese raw silk pricing for the United Kingdom
subfiles.to: J. A. E. Smart, British Embassy, Washington
